drivingQuestion: How can R' Akiva expound the three mentions of גדי to exclude an undomesticated animal, a bird and a non-kosher animal, when those mentions were already expounded for Shmuel's derivations?
outcomeNote: The difficulty stands unanswered at the end of this unit; the answer (קסבר ר' עקיבא איסור חל על איסור) is given in the following unit.

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: חַיָּה וָעוֹף וְכוּ׳. הָנֵי – הָא אַפְּקִינְהוּ לִכְדִשְׁמוּאֵל.
segments.en: § The mishna states: «Rabbi Akiva says:» Cooking the meat of «an undomesticated animal or a bird» in milk is not prohibited by Torah law, as it is stated: “You shall not cook a kid in its mother’s milk” (Exodus 23:19, 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21), three times, excluding an undomesticated animal, a bird, and a non-kosher animal. The Gemara raises a difficulty: Other halakhot have already «been derived from these» mentions of the word “kid,” «in accordance with» the statement «of Shmuel» (see 113b).
